whatIsIt.eli5: The final-answer part, built twice: one copy learns with many helpers per thing, the other learns to give one answer per thing.
whatIsIt.simple: YOLOv10's head. It has two identical sets of branches: one-to-many (trained like YOLOv8, many positives per object) and one-to-one (one positive per object). Only the one-to-one branch is used for final answers, so no NMS is needed. Its class branch is lighter (depthwise convs).
whatIsIt.engineer: Detect with end2end=True: cv2/cv3 (o2m) + deep copies one2one_cv2/one2one_cv3; class branch = Seq(DW3×3 Conv, PW Conv) × 2 → Conv2d(nc). Inference uses o2o outputs + top-k (max_det 300).

whyExists.eli5: Learning with many helpers is easy; answering with one is clean.
whyExists.simple: Consistent dual assignment gives rich training signal and NMS-free inference at the same time. The lighter class branch saves compute because classification needs less capacity than box regression (paper §3.3).
whyExists.engineer: Consistent dual assignments + lightweight classification head (paper §3.1, §3.3).

eli5: Two copies look at the same notes.
The one-answer copy gives the final list.
simple: Both branch sets read P3, P4, P5.
Training: losses on both, with the same matching rule (top-10 vs top-1).
Inference: take the one-to-one predictions, keep the best up to 300.
engineer: o2o branch receives detached features in training (x.detach()).
